subject.title: fix(kill-tree): verify process group leader before using group kill to prevent gateway SIGTERM (#76259)

question: Should OpenClaw accept this helper-side process-group leader check after the branch is rebased onto current main?
rationale: The patch fixes a real gateway SIGTERM path, but it changes shared Unix process cleanup semantics and the current branch conflicts with newer process cleanup changes that must be preserved deliberately.

options.title: Rebase and preserve invariant
options.body: Resolve current-main conflicts, ensure every detached spawn cleanup path still passes `detached: true`, and require focused cleanup proof before merge.

options.title: Accept helper policy as-is after proof
options.body: Maintain the ps/proc leader-check policy if maintainers accept the compatibility tradeoff for omitted `detached` callers.

options.title: Pause for replacement
options.body: If conflict resolution expands beyond this bounded cleanup, pause this PR and use the canonical issue for a narrower replacement branch.

recommendation.title: Rebase and preserve invariant
recommendation.body: Resolve current-main conflicts, ensure every detached spawn cleanup path still passes `detached: true`, and require focused cleanup proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses process-runtime behavior and managed gateway safety, and this history includes adjacent service-managed child detachment work.
